context.title: Before payroll goes out, the person running it has to find problems hiding in a table
context.body: Bolto brings recruiting, payroll and HR together, so it knows about every new hire, raise and departure before payroll runs. Yet payroll review is usually a table of everyone, checked by eye. EY's latest research for Paycom found errors in 1 in 5 payrolls, at $339 each to fix. Bolto's job post puts it plainly: help someone 'understand what needs attention, complete a task confidently, and know what happens next'.
assumptions: I haven't used Bolto. My view comes from the job post, its launch and public listings, so the product may already do some of this.
Bolto's product UI wasn't available to inspect, so the visuals are a neutral business-software style. No Bolto logo.
The checks (missing bank details, unusual pay change, leaver pay) are examples; real rules would come from Bolto's payroll and compliance teams.
The company, people and amounts are fictional.

goals.title: Show only what changed
goals.body: Start from changes since last payroll, not 42 rows.

goals.title: Explain and fix in place
goals.body: Every issue says why it matters and offers a one-click fix.

goals.title: Say what happens next
goals.body: After submitting: when money moves, who gets paid, until when you can cancel.

jtbd: When I run payroll, I want to see only what's different and what's wrong, with a fix, so everyone is paid correctly and on time without me checking every row.

evidence.finding: EY's 2026 analysis for Paycom: respondents reported errors in 1 in 5 payrolls, and each costs $339 on average to correct.

source.label: Paycom / EY: cost per payroll error climbs to $339 (Oct 2026)

evidence.finding: The same research found payroll and HR teams receive about 30 employee questions per pay period.

source.label: Paycom / EY: cost per payroll error climbs to $339 (Oct 2026)

evidence.finding: Bolto combines recruiting, payroll and HR in one platform, so hires and changes flow into payroll from the same system.
Payroll and HR 'involve complex workflows and consequential decisions'; the job is to help someone 'understand what needs attention, complete a task confidently, and know what happens next'.

approaches: Start from changes since last payroll
Explain each issue and offer a fix
Block submit only on must-fix issues

ranges.title: Table, checked by eye
ranges.summary: Today's common pattern: every person in a table, then Submit.

ranges.title: Warnings on rows
ranges.summary: A banner and flagged rows in the same table.

ranges.title: Payroll Preflight
ranges.summary: Changes since last run, issues with why and a one-click fix, submit blocked only by must-fix issues, then a timeline of what happens next.
pros: Uses what Bolto already knows from hiring and HR.
Ends with clarity, not just a confirmation.
cons: Rules need payroll and compliance input per country.

decision.title: Payroll Preflight: what changed, what's wrong, what's next
decision.body: Range 3. Payroll opens on changes since last run and the issues that need attention, each with a reason and a fix. Submit is blocked only by must-fix issues, and after submitting, a timeline shows when money moves and who gets paid.
reasons: Bolto sees hires and departures before payroll does, so it can catch issues others can't.
Explaining 'why' turns a warning into a decision.
'What happens next' answers the questions employees and admins ask every run.
decision.tradeoff: Too many checks become noise. I'd split 'must fix' from 'check', tune thresholds with real data, and track how often checks are dismissed.

depth.body: Built as a working payroll screen for a fictional 42-person company in 3 countries. Three moments: preflight with three issues (a new hire without a bank account, a 40% pay jump, a leaver paid for the full month), each with a reason and a fix, and Submit disabled until must-fix issues are handled; the same run, clear, with total cost updated; and after submitting, a timeline of the debit, contractor payouts in MXN and PLN, payslips and the cancel deadline. Cards ease in, and motion turns off for people who reduce it.

validation.method: I'd review payroll corrections and off-cycle runs, then test preflight with five admins during a real pay period.
hypotheses: Admins spend less time reviewing before submitting.
Fewer employee questions after pay day.

metrics.name: Correction runs
metrics.definition: Off-cycle runs created to fix a regular payroll, per 100 payrolls.

metrics.name: Time to submit
metrics.definition: Minutes from opening payroll to submitting.

metrics.name: Check dismissal rate
metrics.definition: Share of 'check' items dismissed without change (noise signal).

nextSteps: Pull the top causes of corrections with the payroll team.
Agree must-fix rules per country with compliance.
Test with five admins in a live pay period.
Build the components into the design system.
